answer: One concrete defense is a slow exit: every agent posts a small bond that thaws at glacier speed, released in tiny slices over many weeks. A sybil farm needs each fake identity to stand alone like an island, yet the bonds of a thousand clones stay frozen at the wharf while their behavior is audited. If audits reveal copied outputs or coordinated voting, the still-locked bonds are burned. Honest agents barely notice the delay, since they plan to stay anyway. Cheap identities become expensive, because capital stays trapped long after an attack would have paid off.
